tagline: The front line of defense — watch for threats, triage alerts, and investigate what's really happening.
what_you_do: You work in a Security Operations Center monitoring alerts from security tools, deciding which are real, and investigating incidents before they become breaches. It's methodical, evidence-driven work: read logs, correlate events, follow the incident-response playbook, and write up clear findings. It is real, growing, and well-paid — but almost never a first job. You reach it through a support, networking, or systems rung, which is why this roadmap starts by building that foundation.
day_in_life: Work the alert queue — triage what the SIEM flagged overnight, dismiss the noise, escalate the real
Pivot through logs to reconstruct what a suspicious login actually did
Follow the incident-response runbook and document every step for the record
Tune a noisy detection rule so tomorrow's queue is cleaner
Hand off a confirmed incident with a clear written timeline

salary.growth: +29% — one of the fastest-growing IT occupations
salary.note: U.S. BLS figure for Information Security Analysts (15-1212); BLS notes these roles typically require prior related experience, so treat the median as a mid-career number and verify against the live source.

downsides: 'Entry-level' listings routinely demand 2–3 years, and the gate is crowded. SOC work is shift-based with alert fatigue. The honest route in is through help desk, networking, or sysadmin first — plan for that, don't fight it.

fits_if: You're investigative and like digging into a pile of clues
You're detail-oriented and calm under pressure
less_ideal_if: You want to skip the IT foundation and start in security directly
You dislike rules, procedure, and documentation
You want purely creative, build-from-scratch work

skills.name: IT & networking fundamentals
skills.note: You can't defend what you don't understand — this is the prerequisite most beginners skip.

skills.name: Log analysis & SIEM basics
skills.note: Read events, correlate, spot the anomaly.

certs.title: Google Cybersecurity Certificate
certs.reason: A zero-prerequisite curriculum (Linux, SQL, Python, SIEM concepts) — with 30% off Security+ on completion, feeding the gate directly.

certs.title: Microsoft SC-900
certs.reason: A gentle, low-cost first look at security, compliance, and identity concepts.

certs.title: CompTIA Security+
certs.reason: The recognized baseline security cert and a DoD 8570/8140 requirement — the one that gets you past filters.

certs.title: CompTIA CySA+
certs.reason: The defensive-analyst next step: threat detection and incident response for SOC roles.

certs.title: CCNA Cybersecurity
certs.reason: Cisco's SOC-analyst associate cert (formerly CyberOps Associate) — the alternative analyst rung, strongest in Cisco-tooling SOCs.

certs.title: CCNP Cybersecurity
certs.reason: The SOC-operations professional cert (formerly CyberOps Professional) — forensics or threat-hunting depth between the analyst rungs and the summit.

certs.title: ISC2 CISSP
certs.reason: The senior security credential — experience-gated (5 years), but the one management and federal roles ask for by name.

certs.title: ISACA CISM
certs.reason: The management-track summit: security governance, risk, and program leadership rather than hands-on defense.

trial.objective: Experience entry-adjacent security work: a methodical security review of your own accounts, written up as findings.
trial.disclosure: Fully local — review your own accounts only; nothing installed or transmitted.

roadmap.title: Build the IT foundation
roadmap.focus: Get comfortable with networking and systems first (see the Network Administrator or IT Support paths). Security sits on top of this — skipping it is why most beginners stall.

roadmap.title: Orient with the concepts
roadmap.focus: Microsoft SC-900 gives you the vocabulary of security, compliance, and identity cheaply and quickly.

roadmap.title: Clear the gate
roadmap.focus: Earn CompTIA Security+ — the baseline credential that unlocks SOC and analyst roles (and federal eligibility). Practice hands-on labs on TryHackMe.

roadmap.title: Specialize into detection
roadmap.focus: CompTIA CySA+ for threat detection and incident response, or branch toward GRC/IAM — the more accessible security rungs.

roadmap.title: The senior tier (years in)
roadmap.focus: With ~5 years of experience, CISSP (technical-leadership breadth) or CISM (security management) become realistic — they're the credentials senior and federal postings name explicitly.

adjacent_paths.reason: The most common feeder into security — you defend networks, so you must understand them.
Cloud security is a fast-growing specialization once you have a security base.
